svg.text: Digital Wallet — Multi-Raft Event-Sourced CQRS Architecture (1M Transfer TPS = 2M Leg TPS · 99.99% Availability)
Push-Based Reverse Proxy & TC/C Saga Coordinator · Raft-Replicated mmap Event Logs · RocksDB LSM State · S3/HDFS Snapshots
1. Client & Push Reverse Proxy
Wallet Client (1,000,000 TPS)
POST /v1/wallet/balance_transfer
• from_account: "A", to_account: "C"
• amount: "1.00" (string -> BigInt!)
• currency: "USD" (ISO-4217)
• transaction_id: UUIDv7 (idempotent)
Reverse Proxy & TC/C Saga Coord
1. Persists tx in Phase Status Table
2. Dispatches Leg 1 Command (A -$1)
to Partition 1 Raft Leader
3. Receives PUSH receipt from Read
State Machine (0 client polling!)
4. Dispatches Leg 2 Command (C +$1)
(or Cancel A +$1 if Leg 2 fails)
Phase Status Table (Co-Located)
{ tx_id, try_status, phase2,
phase2_status, out_of_order }
• Recovers crashed coordinators
• Blocks late Try after Cancel!
2. Partition 1: Event-Sourced Raft Group (Account A)
Write Path: Command Queue -> Deterministic State Machine
1. Command FIFO Queue (local mmap append-only file)
Commands are external intents; may fail validation (insufficient funds)
2. Deterministic State Machine (Single-Thread Partition Core)
• Zero external I/O, zero wall-clock calls, zero random numbers!
• Reads balance[A] from local RocksDB LSM state cache
• Validates balance[A] >= $1.00 & emits immutable Event: (A, -$1.00)
Raft Consensus Replication (ONLY the Immutable Event List!)
Leader Event Log (mmap) ===> Follower 1 & Follower 2 (Quorum 2/3)
• Why replicate ONLY Events? State & Snapshots are deterministically
derived from Events, while Commands are non-deterministic!
• Guarantees RPO = 0 durability & identical event ordering across nodes
• Local RocksDB LSM applies committed Event to update balance[A]
CQRS Read-Only State Machine + S3/HDFS Binary Snapshots
• Subscribes to committed Event log & builds historical query views
• PUSHES completion receipt directly back to Reverse Proxy!
• Periodic immutable Snapshots saved to S3 Object Lock / HDFS
for fast recovery (Snapshot_t + tail events > t) & point-in-time audit
3. Partition 2 Raft Group (Account C) & 1M TPS Cluster Sizing
Partition 2: Event-Sourced Raft Group (Account C +$1.00)
• Receives Leg 2 Command (C +$1.00) after Partition 1 confirms A -$1.00
• Appends to mmap Command log -> Deterministic State Machine validates
• Replicates Event (C, +$1.00) across Partition 2 Raft Quorum (2/3)
• Applies Event to local RocksDB LSM state (balance[C] += $1.00)
• Read State Machine PUSHES Leg 2 completion to Reverse Proxy
• Reverse Proxy marks Phase Status COMPLETED & returns 200 OK
Quantitative 1M Transfer TPS (= 2M Account-Leg TPS) Sizing
Every transfer mutates 2 accounts (Debit A + Credit C = 2M leg-TPS):
• 100 leg-TPS/node (2PC over WAN) -> 20,000 DB nodes
• 1,000 leg-TPS/node (Cloud RDBMS B-Tree) -> 2,000 DB nodes
• 10,000 leg-TPS/node (mmap + RocksDB ES) -> 200 Raft groups
• 100,000 leg-TPS/node (TigerBeetle/io_uring) -> 20 VSR groups
Three Core Audit Questions Solved by Event Sourcing:
1. Balance at any time T? Replay immutable events up to seq(T).
2. Verify historical & current correctness? Recalculate from genesis.
3. Prove new code version is bug-free? Run new state machine over
historical event log and diff output state against production!
4. Distributed Transaction Deep Dive: Why TC/C Deducts First, Out-of-Order Tombstones & TC/C vs. Saga
Why TC/C Try MUST Deduct (-$1) & Never Credit (+$1)
Choice 1 (VALID): Try: A -$1, C NOP | Confirm: A NOP, C +$1
Choice 2 (INVALID): Try: A NOP, C +$1 | Confirm: A -$1, C NOP
Choice 3 (INVALID): Try: A -$1, C +$1 (requires 2PC atomicity!)
• In TC/C, Phase 1 commits a real local transaction before Phase 2.
• If Try credited C (+$1) before debiting A, user C could withdraw
or spend the phantom $1 before Phase 2 discovers A has $0!
• Deducting A (-$1) in Try freezes funds safely until Confirm/Cancel.
TC/C Out-of-Order Execution (Cancel Before Delayed Try)
• Hazard: Coordinator sends Try(A -$1), times out on slow network,
and sends Cancel(A +$1) which arrives at A's DB BEFORE Try!
• Without defense: Cancel sees no Try (no-op), then delayed Try
arrives and deducts -$1 permanently ("Hanging Try" money loss!)
• Fix: Cancel writes `out_of_order = true` tombstone;
when the delayed Try packet arrives, it checks `out_of_order`
first and aborts immediately without deducting funds!
2PC vs. Try-Confirm/Cancel (TC/C) vs. Orchestrated Saga
2PC (XA): 1 distributed TX; holds row locks across RTTs; SPOF
TC/C: 2 local TXs; Phase 1 Try runs in PARALLEL across shards
• Best when multi-leg latency budget is ultra-tight (< 20 ms)
Orchestrated Saga: Sequential local TXs (T1 -> T2 -> ...)
• On step k failure, executes compensating C_{k-1} ... C_1 backward
• Simpler business-logic state machine than parallel TC/C when
only 2 shards are involved (e.g., Temporal workflow engine)
